findings.description: stats.clear() mutates the single statistics dict shared by every call of the decorated function, instead of giving each call its own dict.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same decorated function at the same time. Mechanism: the first call's clear() empties the dict the second call is still writing to, and both copies write into the same object via copy._local.statistics and self._local.statistics. Impact: statistics such as attempt_number and idle_for are wrong or lost for one or both calls. The previous code rebound a fresh dict per call, so concurrent calls did not share state.

findings.description: stats.clear() reuses one statistics dict across all concurrent invocations of the same async decorated function.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two asyncio tasks await the same decorated coroutine function concurrently. Mechanism: the second call clears the dict the first call is still updating, and both share it through copy._local.statistics. Impact: retry statistics reported to either caller are corrupted, and a caller that kept a reference to the dict from an earlier call sees it reset. The previous code allocated a new dict per call.
